subject: SIG/CAIQ: Clarification on VM rhythm and remediation attestation
messages:
From: Tom Hale <tom.hale@acme.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: Acme Security Team <security@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SIG/CAIQ — VM evidence request and attestation

Olga,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our SIG/CAIQ and internal security review we need concrete evidence of Redwood's vulnerability management posture. Specifically we need:

- A clear summary of scan cadence (external/internal/authenticated vs unauthenticated) and which scans are automated vs scheduled.
- Your SLA commitments by severity (Critical/High/Medium/Low) for CVE remediation or mitigation.
- Any compensating or compensatory controls for longer-lived third-party fixes.
- An attestation we can include in our supplier assessment — a signed statement or DocuSign we can route to our procurement team.

Can you provide a short packet (spreadsheet + one-page SLA statement + attestation) and a contact for follow-ups? We'd like to close this by EOD Fri 2025-07-04 if possible.

Thanks,
Tom Hale
Senior InfoSec Analyst
Acme Corporation
security@acme.com

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 10:03:22 -0700
Subject: Fwd: SIG/CAIQ — VM evidence request and attestation

Ben / Kim — forwarding Tom's ask. They need a compact evidence pack they can attach into their SIG/CAIQ portal and an attestation we can sign. Draft suggestions below; please confirm we can stand behind these numbers and populate the CSV with sample recent scan dates.

Draft commitments (suggestions):
- Scan cadence:
  * External unauthenticated network scan: weekly (automated third-party service)
  * Internal authenticated host scan: nightly (agent-based, aggregated daily)
  * Container image CVE scanning: on build + daily registry sweep
  * Dependency (OSS) scanning: weekly (SCA)
- SLA remediation target windows (time-to-mitigate / time-to-implement compensating control):
  * Critical (RCE/chain-exec): 72 hours from triage assignment
  * High (privilege escalation, auth bypass): 14 days
  * Medium: 45 days
  * Low: addressed in regular maintenance cycles (120 days)
- Compensating controls: automatic WAF rules, host-level microsegmentation, and temporary firewall blocks for externally exploitable issues when fixes require vendor patches.

Attachments I propose to include:
- redwood_vm_scan_matrix.csv (sample rows with last 3 scans per type)
- redwood_remediation_sla_statement.pdf (one-page commitment + signature block)
- vm-attestation-form.pdf (fillable attestation we can sign via DocuSign)

Questions for you: 1) Can we confirm 72h for Critical as our committed SLA? 2) Do we want to call out exceptions (e.g., third-party vendor-managed services where we operate compensating controls and vendor has separate SLA)? 3) Who signs the attestation (Kim, Security lead, or Legal)?

If you both OK this, I'll assemble the files and send to Tom with a DocuSign link.

— Olga
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 11:18:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: SIG/CAIQ — VM evidence request and attestation

Olga — I confirm these commitments. A few clarifications:

- Critical = 72 hours is acceptable for issues we own end-to-end. For third-party products (managed DBs, SaaS dependencies) we will document the compensating control and expected vendor ETA; we should mark those as "vendor-managed" in the CSV.
- Scanning details: internal authenticated scans are agent-based (host agents reporting to our central scanner) with daily aggregation and weekly consolidated reports. External scans use a managed provider (weekly) plus on-demand after major releases.
- We'll include a short note in the PDF about emergency hotfix windows (in some rare cases the mitigation will be to isolate service until a patch is available).

Kim, who should sign the attestation? My vote: Security Lead (Kim) + Redwood Legal CC.

Ben
Sr. Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Hale <tom.hale@acme.com>
Cc: Acme Security Team <security@acme.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Jun 2025 15:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SIG/CAIQ — VM evidence request and attestation

Tom — thanks for the request and timeline. Attached are the items you requested: redwood_vm_scan_matrix.csv (recent scan samples and which scans were authenticated), redwood_remediation_sla_statement.pdf (one-page summary of our remediation windows and compensating controls), and vm-attestation-form.pdf (fillable attestation we can sign).

Key points (high level):
- Scan rhythm: external unauthenticated network scans weekly; internal authenticated host scans aggregated daily (agent-based) with nightly jobs; container image scanning on build + daily registry sweeps; SCA weekly.
- SLA targets: Critical = 72 hours (triage to deployed mitigation/patch), High = 14 days, Medium = 45 days, Low = 120 days. Exceptions: vendor-managed components are documented as vendor-managed with compensating controls and expected vendor timelines noted in the CSV.
- Compensating controls: WAF, dynamic IP blocks, temporary workload isolation, and accelerated patching windows for customer-impacting findings.

We can complete the attestation via DocuSign — routing to Kimberly Park (Security Lead) for signature and Legal on cc. DocuSign request: https://docusign.net/requests/ABC123456789

If you need a redline or more granular evidence for a particular control, let us know which control ID from SIG/CAIQ and we will export the matching artifacts.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_vm_scan_matrix.csv (spreadsheet stub), redwood_remediation_sla_statement.pdf (PDF stub), vm-attestation-form.pdf (fillable PDF stub)
